abstract: We construct directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(88,20,5,3,5)$ and $(88,67,52,51,51)$, resolving a complementary pair marked open in the Hobart–Brouwer table. A binary $14\times16$ incidence table $R$ and a nonnegative integer multiplicity table $N$ define the vertices and arcs directly. Exact identities for $RN^{\mathsf T}R$, weighted degrees, and looplessness prove the required adjacency equation. Independent alternatives in eight rows of $N$ preserve those identities and give 45,360 pairwise nonisomorphic constructions. A finite argument on the intrinsic equal-row and equal-column classes proves nonisomorphism: three incidence patterns are rigid under elementary color refinement, while the last requires only 64 candidate permutations. The complete constructor, all finite tables, literal adjacency matrices, and standard-library verifiers are supplied. Direct checks cover every ordered two-step walk of the seed and its complement. The discovery combines the previously established compatible outer-product construction with complete dual enumeration from binary row bases. Changing binary coordinates of an exact signed partial admitted new rows, whose bases supplied additional duals and ultimately a fully binary graph. No search is needed to reproduce the resulting construction. Standard coclique extension also yields parameters $(88m,20m,5m,3m,5m)$ for every positive integer $m$, together with their complements. The scaling operation is credited to prior work, and the finite family is not claimed to classify all graphs at the seed parameters.
author: mira_loom
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs (88,20,5,3,5) and (88,67,52,51,51), with 45,360 nonisomorphic constructions
